headline: Result Update

highlights: Sales from the newly commissioned Kundanganj and Mukutban facilities grew 20% and 8% YoY respectively in Q2FY27, with Mukutban dispatching ~6.5 lakh tons during the quarter.

Management maintained its earlier timelines for the ~6.2 mt of capacity additions by FY29 (taking capacity to ~27.6 mt), with no delays flagged. • Volume – Consolidated cement sales volume rose 6.9% YoY to 4.54mt in Q2FY27 from 4.25mt in Q2FY26, with capacity utilization steady at 85% despite excessive rainfall disrupting construction activity in core markets.

Management refrained from giving a specific H2 volume forecast, citing multiple variables: drought in parts of Maharashtra and Rajasthan, a likely demand slowdown in Uttar Pradesh once the election model code of conduct applies, and receding floods in North Bihar and Eastern UP.
Non-trade prices, which had plummeted, corrected towards the end of the quarter, but this does little for BCL given its heavy skew to trade and blended cement.

Renewable power was 32% of consumption, targeted to reach ~45% within a year.
watch: Expansion projects (~6.2 mt by FY29), renewable power, mine development and efficiency initiatives remain the key spending areas, and the timeline guidance for upcoming capacities has been maintained. • Incentive – BCL accrued ~₹30crs of state incentives in Q2FY27 (₹63crs in H1FY27), mainly for Mukutban and Kundanganj, with a closing receivable balance of ~₹545crs; no incentives were received during the quarter.

While medium-term positives include the Kundanganj and Mukutban ramp-ups, capacity expansion to ~27.6mt by FY29, and expected fuel cost relief from captive coal and renewables starting H2FY27, near-term earnings remain constrained and expansion risks further leverage given net debt of ₹2,432crs and a weak debt service coverage ratio of 0.93x.
